title: Indoor Microclimate Monitoring Optimization in Heritage Buildings: The Bologna University Library Case Study
content: The paper aims to describe the methodology and to interpret the results of an experimental study on the indoor microclimatic conditions of the University Library of Bologna (BUL), a very relevant cultural heritage building in the historic city centre. During the past few years, the way the Library's spaces have been used and managed has changed from the classical activities of an historical library, limited to the preservation and consultation of materials, to a greater enhancement and valorization of the premises, particularly the Great Hall. To better understand the impact of these extended uses and to gain further updated insights, a monitoring campaign has started in September 2024, funded by the ECOSYSTER project, part of the Italian National Recovery and Resilience Plan (in the context of the NextGenerationEU). The objective of the monitoring project is the knowledge of the specific microclimatic conditions and the historical climate of the three main rooms of the BUB, in order to define (a) the alert ranges in case of microclimate risk; (b) the choices and methods of management and use of the different rooms; and (c) the right balance between the needs of conservation and the thermal comfort of staff, users and visitors; (d) the link between the assessed thermal conditions and the energy consumption optimization strategies.
